headline: IBM's new quantum chip foundry Anderon plans to manufacture quantum processors for other companies, backed by a US award of up to $1 billion.
score_reason: The award dates from 16 Sep 2026 and the facts come from a 7 Oct report, so this is background rather than new.
importance_line: Makers of quantum chips without their own factory may gain a shared supplier, but Anderon still has to prove its yields and win customers beyond IBM.
summary: IEEE Spectrum reports that Anderon, a quantum chip foundry set up by IBM in Albany, New York, is backed by a finalised US Commerce Department award of up to $1 billion, announced on 16 Sep 2026, matched by $1 billion from IBM. It aims to build quantum chips for outside designers much as TSMC does for conventional chips, with wafers promised to customers by the end of the year and Rigetti Computing among those in talks.
notes: The Forbes article chosen by the curator was blocked (403); facts come from IEEE Spectrum, 7 Oct 2026, on the same subject. A foundry is a factory that makes chips designed by others.
